text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.6% today to $142.28, continuing a three-day rally that's recovered most of last week's losses. The stock has climbed $5.70 in the past four days as oil prices stabilized—US crude is holding around $89.62 per barrel and global oil at $92.14—after falling sharply earlier in the week. The bounce appears tied to energy markets finding a floor rather than company-specific news; the most recent mention was a general market call on November 11th, before this recovery began.

The broader energy sector is dealing with conflicting signals: heating oil prices are up 59% from last winter (which can support refining margins), but Russian crude production has rebounded to over 8.7 million barrels per day, pushing global oil into surplus territory. That supply overhang is likely what knocked oil and the stock down last week, and today's gain reflects a temporary stabilization rather than a fundamental shift in the supply-demand picture.
